The Federal Convention , also known as the Federal Assembly ( German : Bundesversammlung [ˈbʊndəsfɛɐ̯ˌzamlʊŋ] ⓘ ), is, together with the Joint Committee , one of two non-permanent constitutional bodies in the institutional framework of the Federal Republic of Germany . It is convened solely for the purpose of electing the president of Germany . The Federal Convention consists of all members of the federal parliament ( Bundestag ) and the same number of delegates from the 16 federated states . Those delegates are elected by the state parliaments for this purpose only.
